Operation 'listAvailableSlots' has semantic quality issues: vague_summary, missing_input_details, poor_ai_interpretability. Original summary 'List available start times' is too generic. data.current_description: Available start times for an event type, as UTC instants, after availability, calendar conflicts, buffers, notice and daily limits have been applied. The range may span at most 31 days. Invite-only event types are included, because the caller owns them. from and to are UTC dates, not the host's: the window runs from 00:00:00Z on from to 23:59:59Z on to. For a host whose time zone is behind UTC that is not the same as their calendar day — asking for one date returns the tail of the previous local evening and omits the end of the one you asked for — so widen the range by a day either side and filter the returned instants in the zone you care about.
data.summary_suggestion: Get available booking slots for an event type
data.description_suggestion: Returns available start times (UTC instants) for booking an event type, after applying availability rules, calendar conflicts, buffers, notice periods, and daily limits. Accepts from and to parameters as UTC dates (inclusive range from 00:00:00Z to 23:59:59Z). Maximum range is 31 days. Note: from and to are UTC dates, not the host's local dates; for hosts in UTC-behind time zones, widen the date range by one day on each side and filter results to the desired time zone. Invite-only event types are included.

data.current_description: Starts delivering again to a subscription that was switched off after a long run of failures, keeping its id and its signing secret. Without this an integration can only delete the subscription and create another, which issues a new secret — so anything that stored the old one starts rejecting every delivery as unsigned. Returns the subscription either way: calling it on one that is already active changes nothing and is not an error.

data.current_description: Starts delivering again to a subscription that was switched off after a long run of failures, keeping its id and its signing secret. Without this an integration can only delete the subscription and create another, which issues a new secret — so anything that stored the old one starts rejecting every delivery as unsigned. Returns the subscription either way: calling it on one that is already active changes nothing and is not an error.

Returns the subscription object with updated status. Calling this on an already-active subscription is safe and returns the subscription unchanged; the operation is idempotent.

data.current_description: Available start times for an event type, as UTC instants, after availability, calendar conflicts, buffers, notice and daily limits have been applied. The range may span at most 31 days. Invite-only event types are included, because the caller owns them. from and to are UTC dates, not the host's: the window runs from 00:00:00Z on from to 23:59:59Z on to. For a host whose time zone is behind UTC that is not the same as their calendar day — asking for one date returns the tail of the previous local evening and omits the end of the one you asked for — so widen the range by a day either side and filter the returned instants in the zone you care about.

Accepts from and to parameters as UTC dates (range max 31 days). Returns times as UTC; note that for hosts in timezones behind UTC, the local calendar day may not align with the UTC date range. Invite-only event types are included. Useful for populating booking calendars and availability pickers.
